title: SYSK Selects: The Star Wars Holiday Special of 1978
summary: Selects rerun of the Stuff You Should Know episode on the 1978 Star Wars Holiday Special. Josh introduces it as a holiday pick and the hosts cover Life Day, the Wookiee celebration, and the background of the special: George Lucas's request for a Wookiee-focused story, CBS's push for a variety show format, and the hired writers, performers and directors. They walk through the plot (Han Solo and Chewbacca trying to reach Kazook for Life Day while the Wookiee family waits and the Empire raids their home), the guest stars and odd segments (Harvey Korman, Bea Arthur, Art Carney, Diahann Carroll, Jefferson Starship, the Boba Fett cartoon), and the special's poor reception, ratings, and Lucas's later comments. The episode ends with listener mail about the Voynich Manuscript.

segments.title: Opening banter and Life Day introduction
segments.summary: Josh introduces the episode as a SYSK Selects pick for the holidays. The hosts joke about Star Wars Day and opening-night tickets, then explain Life Day, the Wookiee holiday held every three years, and why the special is widely derided.

segments.title: Origins of the special and George Lucas's Wookiee idea
segments.summary: After the first Star Wars film's success, CBS executives proposed a TV special. Lucas wanted a story set on Kazook, the Wookiee homeworld, which had been cut from Empire Strikes Back. He had a forty-page Wookiee Bible. The hosts describe the hiring of writers Bruce Vilanch and Lenny Rips and the husband-and-wife producers.

segments.title: Variety show format and production troubles
segments.summary: The special was built as a variety show even though the format was going stale by 1978. Director David Acord left after a few segments and Steve Binder finished the job. The hosts describe the cast's reluctance, Harrison Ford's on-camera reaction, and the writers' idea of wordless Wookiee dialogue.

segments.title: Plot, Wookiee dialogue, and guest stars
segments.summary: The plot follows Han Solo and Chewbacca trying to reach Kazook for Life Day while the family waits. The hosts describe the ten minutes of untranslated Wookiee speech, the family members' names, and the Imperial blockade. They note Lucas's reaction to the writers' dialogue ideas.

segments.title: Musical numbers, cantina scene, and odd segments
segments.summary: The hosts describe the special's guest stars and strange segments: Harvey Korman as a cooking show host and other roles, Bea Arthur singing last call at the cantina, Art Carney as a trader, a virtual-reality hair dryer porn-like scene with Diahann Carroll, and a long Jefferson Starship music video played on a hologram while Imperial guards ransack the house.

segments.title: Boba Fett cartoon segment
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the animated segment Lumpy watches, which introduces Boba Fett and features Luke, R2-D2 and C-3PO, and which was widely seen as the special's best part. It was removed from the official version for copyright reasons.

segments.title: Ending, Life Day finale, and Princess Leia's song
segments.summary: Han and Chewbacca return, and a stormtrooper dies after tripping over logs and falling from a balcony. The special closes with a Life Day ceremony where Princess Leia gives a speech and sings a song, which the hosts describe as the point where she seems to be on drugs.

segments.title: Reception, ratings, and Lucas's later comments
segments.summary: The special aired in November 1978 and drew about 13 million viewers in the US, finishing second in its hours. Critics, fans, and cast disliked it. Lucas later distanced himself from it and was said to have considered releasing it on DVD, and Carrie Fisher reportedly wanted a clean copy for commentary.

segments.title: Final thoughts and resources
segments.summary: The hosts give their final thoughts, recommend Vanity Fair's Han Solo Comedy Hour article, the book How Star Wars Conquered the Universe, and the Mystery Science Theater 3000 commentary, and mention HowStuffWorks Star Wars articles.

segments.title: Listener mail: Voynich Manuscript
segments.summary: A listener writes about the Voynich Manuscript episode, suggesting its language could be shaped by familiar linguistic structures and that the manuscript's origins might be less exotic. The listener also says the podcast helps with noise and commutes.
